Confidence is Medium for this bounded synthesis, not full forecast acceptance.

facts.label: Integrated implication
facts.text: The prior thesis survives but becomes more conditional: installed-product replacement economics, qualification friction and observed margins support debt service, while debt-funded extraction can prevent those strengths benefiting creditors. The reference and upside support operating resilience; persistent downside coverage below 3x shifts monitoring toward cash interest and allocation before headline leverage. Positive cash proxies do not establish funded obligations or accessible liquidity. [P Findings; F T2H.7–8]

facts.label: Integrated implication
facts.text: The strongest countercase combines installed-base demand, original growth guidance, positive historical/Q1 operations, historical financing execution and documented fixed coupons/hedges. It would strengthen the conclusion if margins survive recurring integration/remuneration costs, collections translate earnings into retained accessible cash, actual debt payments occur and dated funding is documented. Conversely, larger adjustments without cash, inventory absorption, new debt-financed distributions or failed access verification would weaken it—even with revenue growth. No issuer retention commitment or leverage target/date is supplied. [P Findings; F T2H.8]

spans.text: ## Request

View: TDG’s operating resilience remains supported, but the conditional forecast makes interest-service vulnerability more immediate and restricts confidence in creditor improvement from cash accumulation. The downside reaches the 3x coverage watch in FY2025 despite declining carrying leverage; capital retention, not earnings growth alone, remains decisive. Confidence is Medium for this bounded synthesis, not full forecast acceptance.

This incremental CP-2 consumption uses deploy-v-r14’s prior live CP-2 adaptation for run `sol-remaining-tdg-forecast-consumer-20261105`, executed **2026-11-05**. Historical as-of remains **2024-09-30**; November guidance and December context are separately dated subsequent evidence. Scope is consolidated TransDigm Group Incorporated, including controlled subsidiaries, not a guarantor-only assessment. This is neither new full underwriting nor a second native-contract execution. No rating, covenant-breach finding, refinancing guarantee, recovery outcome or probability is assigned.

## Findings
### Forecast adoption
| Finding | Evidence and period | Effect on credit view | Boundary |

| Reference supports conditional improvement | FY2025–27 coverage rises 3.138498x to 3.762659x; carrying leverage falls 5.096956x to 4.235896x. [F T2H.6/8] | Supports the historical earnings buffer, but only under retention and payment assumptions. | USD1000m annual repayment is commanded; no cash sweep. Cash rebuilding is not additional debt-paydown evidence. |

| Downside prioritizes interest risk | Coverage is 2.282544x in FY2025 and remains below 3x through FY2027; carrying leverage ends at 5.294869x. [F T2H.6–8] | Makes service resilience the earliest calculable watch, ahead of a 7x leverage hit. | A 20% earnings haircut holds revenue unchanged; the 10% interest increase is uncalibrated, not a sales shock or legal trigger. |

| Moving and static tests differ legitimately | No moving-model 7x hit; F retains CP-2A’s combined static 7x/3x crossing. [F T2H.7] | Static vulnerability remains relevant; the moving result does not invalidate it. | September debt and USD1158m historical cash interest differ from forward earnings, closing-debt repayments and opening-debt interest at 6%. |

| Upside is substantive counterevidence | Margin 0.5494 yields FY2027 coverage 3.904807x and cash USD6594.596095m. [F T2H.4/6/8] | Cash-backed margin delivery could materially strengthen the view. | Same sales and repayment; improved margins do not accelerate debt reduction without a sweep. |

| Guidance anchors, not validates, the engine | November 7, 2024 exact FY2025 midpoints: sales USD8850m, EBITDA As Defined USD4685m; ordinary EBITDA USD4479m. [F T2H.2/3, research adoption] | Supports an operating reference, not an accepted central cash forecast. | Finite growth 0.1146/margin 0.5294 produce USD8849.924m/USD4685.1497656m. Guidance net interest USD1540m and tax provision USD616m are not cash drivers. |

| Actual allocation limits forecast adoption | December 28, 2024 cash USD2459m and carrying debt USD25049m; Q1 OCF USD752m, distributions USD4396m, repurchases USD316m, securitization proceeds USD163m and option proceeds USD35m. [F T2H.2/8] | Positive operations coexist with extraction: retention cannot be inferred. | Incomplete USD4348m annual distribution stipulation excludes other financing/payouts. Q1’s 89 days versus 91 comparative days are not annualized; October USD4348m/4347m precision conflict remains unresolved. |
### Integrated implication

The prior thesis survives but becomes more conditional: installed-product replacement economics, qualification friction and observed margins support debt service, while debt-funded extraction can prevent those strengths benefiting creditors. The reference and upside support operating resilience; persistent downside coverage below 3x shifts monitoring toward cash interest and allocation before headline leverage. Positive cash proxies do not establish funded obligations or accessible liquidity. [P Findings; F T2H.7–8]

The strongest countercase combines installed-base demand, original growth guidance, positive historical/Q1 operations, historical financing execution and documented fixed coupons/hedges. It would strengthen the conclusion if margins survive recurring integration/remuneration costs, collections translate earnings into retained accessible cash, actual debt payments occur and dated funding is documented. Conversely, larger adjustments without cash, inventory absorption, new debt-financed distributions or failed access verification would weaken it—even with revenue growth. No issuer retention commitment or leverage target/date is supplied. [P Findings; F T2H.8]
### Monitoring
| Trigger | Credit mechanism | Required action |
| Coverage approaches/below 3x; delivery or cash-margin miss | Less interest cushion and retained cash | Refresh earnings/service bridge; challenge uncommitted extraction. |
| New payouts, deals or missed USD1000m assumed repayment | Policy overwhelms modeled improvement | Replace exclusions with dated sources/uses; distinguish actual payments from assumptions. |

| March 31/September 30, 2025 hedge transitions; July 11, 2025 securitization expiry | Reset/settlement and renewal dependence | Verify historically dated terms and outcomes separately; infer neither renewal nor failure. |

| Restrictions, draw conditions or cash trough emerge | Positive annual cash may be inaccessible when needed | Obtain weekly/monthly treasury bridge, access certificates and minimum cash requirement. |
Monitoring dates are historical-calendar checkpoints, not upcoming events as of execution. [F T2H.7–8]

## Gaps

Accessible liquidity, runway and minimum-liquidity test remain **Not calculable: access/minimum cash evidence missing**; annual-end lows are not intra-year troughs. Model CFO/FCF are simplified proxies using 10% combined tax/WC and 2% capex assumptions, not normalized GAAP cash forecasts. Separate taxes/WC, maintenance capex, acquired/organic earnings and accepted quality EBITDA remain unresolved. [F G1–4/11]

Opening debt is USD24880m carrying, not USD25002m broader known claims. Finance leases/securitization are embedded; operating leases USD62m, pension USD19m and remediation USD41m do not become immediate debt or cash deductions. Avoid duplicate reserve/settlement costs. [F T2H.2; Calculations]

The 6% rate and 10% shock lack calibration. Term-loan no-floor evidence does not resolve qualified hedge coverage; neither USD91.89m gross sensitivity nor issuer USD30m sensitivity may be added again. Ownership/support, legal capacity, platform concentration and source-representation conflicts remain restricted. [P Gaps; F Calculations/Gaps]

Native January–December wrapper incompatibility remains unresolved. Preserve October–September fiscal dates; pure conditional controls do not imply native acceptance. Missing segment mappings and complete financing schedules prevent renderer-ready forecast claims. [F G8–11]
